take_homes: Don't pick a checker by reputation. Run several on the same output, score them, keep the one that wins, and write down what it misses.
A citation can be real and still not say the thing (citation cargo-cult). That's a failure mode I hadn't named.
Have a separate worker generate the bad test output so the main session stays blind, and re-read the file after an edit instead of trusting the agent's report.

monday.move: Rebuild the four-detector benchmark on one real agent output from our own pipeline (probably a customer-facing summary), and have a teammate run it with me
monday.when: Tuesday afternoon, not Monday, because Monday is sprint planning
monday.stop_condition: If the scorer's own adjudication disagrees with a human spot-check on more than a handful of the 30 claims, I stop trusting the scoreboard
monday.blocker: I don't have a labelled reference set, and the scorer is an LLM, so I'm not sure whose judgment the scoreboard actually rests on

misconception.why: Seeing four detectors catch different things made me doubt that 'fine' output is fine. But I'd still skip checking on low-stakes stuff, and I never saw the actual numbers in this run.

one_line: Good if your team has never measured a checker, and the 'run four, keep the winner' idea is worth it, but the first half is slow for anyone who already runs agents.
